title: A Mixtape for the Scholarship
premise: Lena Villalobos, a scholarship student at Ashgrove Academy, survives on invisibility until she finds coded directions hidden in her late grandmother's recipe box — instructions that lead to a sealed archive proving the academy's founding families erased a community, including her own, to build their legacy. The 'championships' are rituals: the public academic games that distract everyone, and the secret rite where the heirs of the founders renew the pact that keeps the erasure buried. To expose the truth without losing her scholarship or her found family, Lena must enter both contests, win the one nobody watches, and choose at graduation between belonging on their terms or burning the archive and building something new. She wins the hidden championship by refusing it, releasing the memory back to the town.
about_author: Cyrus Galloway is a former debate coach who grew up in a mill town swallowed by a private academy and never quite got over it. He writes stories about kids who are too busy surviving to notice they're the protagonists.

chapters.title: Fine Is a Full-Time Job
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Establishes her double life: tutoring rich classmates, eating lunch in the library, sending money home. When her grandmother dies, Lena inherits a battered recipe box and finds a card labeled 'For the ones who remember' with coordinates instead of ingredients. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into curiosity.

chapters.title: Cardamom, Salt, and a Locked Door
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Following the first 'recipe,' she discovers a maintenance tunnel beneath the chapel holding a wall of confiscated student belongings spanning decades — including a jacket with her family name. She's nearly caught by Theo Marsh, golden-boy heir to a founder family, who covers for her for reasons he won't explain. Beat: dread mixed with the first crack in her isolation.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The Founders' Games — the loud, televised academic competition — begin, and Theo explains its real function: spectacle. He recruits Lena as his team's wildcard, half-ally, half-hostage. She realizes winning gives her access to restricted archives. Beat: uneasy alliance, mutual suspicion laced with attraction.

chapters.title: Recipes for Forgetting
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Decoding more cards with her best friend Priya, Lena learns each 'dish' corresponds to a ritual the heirs perform to renew the pact — and that her grandmother was once an Ashgrove student who refused. A threatening note appears in Lena's locker: 'Some recipes ruin the cook.' Beat: fear hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Heirs and Heirlooms
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Midterm gala: Lena infiltrates the founders' wing, overhears Headmistress Vane and the heirs planning this year's renewal rite, and learns the championship winner traditionally becomes the next vessel of the pact. Theo catches her listening — and lies to protect her. Beat: betrayal and tenderness colliding.

chapters.title: What Grandma Burned
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A trip home uncovers her mother's complicity: she knew and chose silence so Lena could have the scholarship. Mother-daughter confrontation about survival versus memory. Lena decides she can want both — to belong AND to tell the truth. Beat: the book's thematic heart.

chapters.title: The Games Turn Cruel
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Vane, suspecting Lena, rigs the semifinals against her and gets Priya suspended on fabricated cheating charges. Theo must publicly denounce Lena to keep his own family safe — and does. Beat: rock bottom; allies scattered, scholarship threatened, loneliness total.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box Opens
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The final card reveals the rite's location and cost: the champion's memories of the erased community are consumed to seal it again. Lena realizes her grandmother didn't fail — she hid the counter-recipe inside the box itself, waiting for someone with nothing left to lose. Beat: quiet, fierce clarity.

chapters.title: The Championship That Does
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating Lena and Theo. At the midnight rite, Lena lets herself be crowned champion, then reads the counter-recipe aloud, unbinding the pact as the archive floods open and the town's stolen history pours out. Theo turns against his family to hold the door. Vane falls; the heirs scatter. Beat: triumphant, costly chaos.

chapters.title: A Mixtape for Everyone
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, epilogue at graduation. Ashgrove opens its archives and scholarships to the town; Priya returns exonerated; Theo, disowned, starts over. Lena records a mixtape of the songs from the cards and leaves it in the recipe box for whoever needs remembering next. Final beat: belonging chosen, not granted.
